name: Extreme heat
summary: No heatwave warning across a major region found on 27 Nov; recent heat in Brazil and Queensland has eased
state: Brazil's Inmet recorded 39.8°C at Porto Murtinho on 13 Nov, but said the heat did not meet its heatwave definition (Latin Times, 16 Nov). Far North Queensland's severe heatwave, with Weipa above 36°C for 41 straight days, ran to 19 Nov (The Watchers). Searches on 27 Nov found no current top-tier heat warning across a major region, no new national record and no deadly heatwave, so Normal holds.
for_you: Southern-hemisphere summer is starting, so heat warnings in Australia, South America and southern Africa become more likely. Travellers should check local met service warnings and FCDO travel advice before trips.
rubric_hit: Normal: no major heatwave affecting large populations as of 27 Nov

sources.title: Latin Times — Brazil heat surge: temperatures near 40C in November

why: Heat is the deadliest weather hazard globally, straining power grids, crops and health systems.
drivers: Heat domes, climate warming, season, humidity, urban heat islands.

rubric.alert: Deadly heatwave with top-tier official warnings across a large population.
rubric.watch: Heatwave warnings across a major region, or national temperature records.
rubric.normal: No major heatwaves affecting large populations.
